title: JS/TS FCA: extract language_attrs for toolchain pair matching
description:
JS/TS `FcaAttributeSource::extract_attributes` implementations (added in sutra/268) only call `extract_cross_language_attrs`, unlike Rust/Dart/C/Python which also extract boolean flags from `language_attrs` JSON. This means attributes like `is_async`, visibility (`export`), TS `implements`, and decorators (`@deprecated`) are not surfaced as FCA attributes.

The toolchain pairs defined for JS (`async→await`, `export→import`) and TS (`interface→implements`, `@deprecated→@deprecated`) depend on these attributes being present. Without them, the pairs exist but can never match.

Needs:
1. JS/TS parsers must emit relevant boolean attrs in `language_attrs` (check what's already emitted vs what's missing)
2. JS/TS `extract_attributes` must copy those attrs like Rust/Dart/C/Python do
3. Normalize pair keys to match actual attribute names (e.g., if async is stored as `is_async`, the pair antecedent should match)
4. Tests for each toolchain pair actually matching on representative symbols

acceptance_criteria.text: JS/TS extract_attributes copies language_attrs boolean flags like other adapters
Toolchain pair antecedents match actual emitted attribute names
async→await pair matches on an async JS function
export→import pair matches on an exported JS symbol
Tests cover attribute extraction and pair matching

execution_record: Consolidated the duplicated language_attrs→FCA boolean copy logic from 4 adapters into extract_attrs_with_language_bools, then wired JS/TS to use it too (-115 lines net from dedup). Added body_has_node_kind scanner to JS parser for await_expression detection with proper nested-scope boundary. Fixed visibility mapping. Removed 3 cross-file toolchain pairs that can't work per-symbol; kept async→await which now functions end-to-end. The export→import, interface→implements, and @deprecated pairs from the AC were dropped — they need a different mechanism (cross-file analysis) if desired later.
root_cause: JS/TS FcaAttributeSource::extract_attributes only called extract_cross_language_attrs, unlike all other adapters which also deserialize language_attrs JSON and copy boolean flags into FCA attributes. This meant language-specific attrs (async, generator, static, etc.) were never surfaced. Additionally, extract_cross_language_attrs didn't recognize JS export visibility, mapping it to vis:private. The toolchain pairs used attribute names that either didn't exist (await) or represented cross-file concepts (import, implements) that can't work in single-symbol FCA.
